impact: A cyberattack has hit three regional blood banks in France, disrupting systems used to monitor and control refrigerated storage facilities. The incident took place overnight between Sunday and Monday, at roughly the same time hackers were targeting supermarket refrigeration systems across several European countries. Those attacks forced retailers to discard large quantities of food after hackers interfered with cooling and freezer systems.

impact: Crédit Mutuel Arkéa said in a press notice that the attackers were able to make transfers using the bank’s own account after compromising an unnamed supplier. ZachXBT estimated the size of the theft at more than $133 million, based on withdrawals from cryptocurrency exchange accounts and transactions intending to launder the assets. It described the hack as “sophisticated” and not the result of human error, without providing additional details. “The attackers used Crédit Mutuel Arkéa’s own account to carry out transactions to other banking institutions, which then potentially allowed them to convert this money into cryptocurrency via specialised platforms,” according to the statement.
